summary: Albania is one of Europe's most open destinations — citizens of the EU, UK, US and dozens more countries enter visa-free for 90 days in any 180 (US passport holders may stay a full year), and most other nationalities can apply online for an e-Visa or enter visa-free with a valid multiple-entry Schengen, UK or US visa.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Albania?
faq.answer: Most travelers do not. Citizens of the EU, UK, US, Canada, Australia, Japan and dozens of other countries enter visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period (US citizens may stay up to a year). If your passport does need a visa, you can usually apply online at e-visa.al, or enter visa-free if you hold a valid multiple-entry Schengen, UK or US visa.

faq.question: How long can US citizens stay in Albania?
faq.answer: Up to one year visa-free — one of the most generous allowances anywhere in Europe. Stays beyond that require a residence permit from the local authorities.

faq.question: Can I enter Albania with a Schengen visa?
faq.answer: Yes, for most nationalities. A valid multiple-entry Schengen, EU, UK or US visa that you have already used in the country that issued it (or a Schengen, EU, UK or US residence permit) lets otherwise visa-required nationalities enter Albania visa-free; leave at least 3 days before it expires. Single-entry Schengen visas do not qualify, and the exemption does not apply to Iranian citizens.

faq.question: Is Albania in the Schengen Area or the EU?
faq.answer: No — Albania is an EU candidate country but belongs to neither the EU nor Schengen. Days spent in Albania do not count against your 90/180-day Schengen allowance, which makes it a popular stop for long-term travelers around Europe.

faq.question: What currency is used in Albania, and can I pay in euros?
faq.answer: The Albanian lek (ALL). Euros are widely accepted in tourist areas but usually at an unfavourable rate — withdraw or exchange lek for day-to-day spending, and keep cash on hand outside the main cities.
